title: Can LLMs Help Allocate Public Health Resources? A Case Study on Childhood Lead Testing

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM resource allocation recommendations by prompting models to distribute lead test kits across city neighborhoods and comparing their prioritized lists against an empirical Priority Score that incorporates public health coverage rates (a proxy for socioeconomic vulnerability), lead prevalence, and testing gaps.

Analyzing model outputs to identify heuristic biases where LLMs favor neighborhoods with visible demographic factors (such as higher population density) or non-empirical narratives over empirically measured exposure risks in marginalized communities.
